designedFor: DESIGN.md §8 (openbanking-platform, locked 2026-11-10) — catalog data only. No generator run, no repo touched.

$meta.purpose: Everything in this fragment is derivable by ONE template into: api/openapi.yaml (JSON-schema'd), a Flyway db/migration, a repository, a rules component with generated tests, and api/events.yaml (AsyncAPI). Nothing here needs a human to interpret it. Where something could NOT be made mechanical it is listed under the domain's `uncertain`, not smuggled in as a field.

id.note: control-record identifier; primary key when listed in controlRecord.primaryKey

ref.note: cross-service reference carrying `refDomain`. NEVER a Postgres FOREIGN KEY: each service domain owns its own schema. Referential integrity is the caller's, asserted by contract tests, not the DB.

enum.note: `values` is mandatory. `const` pins it to one value and also emits a DEFAULT + single-value CHECK.

money.note: SIGNED minor units, never a float, never a BigDecimal on the wire. Field name MUST end `Minor` (estate precedent: bian-services/sd-current-account amountMinor/balanceMinor/availableMinor). The record's `currency` field supplies the ISO 4217 exponent; the exponent is NOT always 2 (BHD/KWD/OMR/TND = 3, JPY = 0), so no generated code may multiply or divide by 100. All money fields of a record are named again in controlRecord.money.

ratio.note: EXACT ratio. Used for profit-sharing ratios, weightages and every rate. Never a float, never a double, never a percentage string. `maxDenominator` (default 1000000) is emitted as a CHECK so that cross-multiplication in the rules component cannot overflow int64.

currency.note: ISO 4217 alpha-3. The generator emits a CHECK against the committed ISO 4217 table, which carries the exponent.

$meta.noNestedStructures: There is deliberately no object or array field type. A repeating or nested structure is a behaviourQualifier, which the template renders as its own table (`<cr.table>_<bq.table>`, parent column `<cr.primaryKey>`), its own sub-resource path (`/v1/{crSlug}/{crId}/{bqSlug}`) and its own schema. This is what keeps one catalog field = one column = one OpenAPI property, which is the whole reason the 49th domain costs one data entry.
$meta.tableNames: Every controlRecord and behaviourQualifier carries an explicit short `table`. Derivation from the BIAN control-record name would collide: `mudarabah_investment_account_fulfillment_arrangement` + `_investment_mandate` is 70 characters and Postgres truncates identifiers at 63, silently merging two tables. The explicit name is not decoration.

assertLanguage.note: Deliberately tiny and closed so that `assert` compiles to a Java guard, a Postgres CHECK or a generator-time lint with no interpretation.
identifiers: bq.<bqTable>.<fieldName> (a row of a behaviour qualifier)
prior.<fieldName> (the pre-update value, service-enforced rules only)

functions.absent(f): field NOT declared on this control record — generator-lint only; evaluated against the catalog entry at stamping time, never at runtime
functions.sum(bq.<t>.<f>): int64 sum over all rows of that behaviour qualifier for this control record
functions.ratioAdd(a, b): exact: (a.num*b.den + b.num*a.den) / (a.den*b.den), compared by cross-multiplication — no division is ever performed
functions.ratioMul(amountMinor, r): int64 exact multiply-then-divide: (amountMinor * r.numerator) / r.denominator, TRUNCATED TOWARD ZERO. The discarded remainder is never silently absorbed — every rule that uses ratioMul in a money identity also carries an explicit residual field.

assertLanguage.rounding: There is exactly one rounding point in this business area: the allocation of an int64 distributable profit across N accounts. It is explicit (roundingResidualMinor on the distribution run) and bounded by a rule. No other generated money path rounds.

ruleShape.id: stable, quoted in the generated test name and in the error payload
ruleShape.assert: must hold; the generated code rejects or flags when it does not
ruleShape.onViolation: reject | flag  (the only two values DESIGN.md §8 allows)
ruleShape.enforcedAt: db-check (a CHECK in the Flyway migration) | service (a guard in the rules component + a generated test) | generator-lint (asserted against the catalog entry when the repo is stamped; a violation fails generation, not a request)
ruleShape.errorCode: emitted into the OpenAPI error enum and the generated deny-test
ruleShape.citation: the external standard the rule comes from, or the explicit word UNSOURCED
ruleShape.test: present on every money-identity and ratio rule: concrete int64 inputs for the generated test, so the test is real rather than aspirational

$meta.sharedAccountBase: The five account domains share 17 identical fields (accountId … updatedAt). They are written out per domain on purpose: the catalog is data, and a shared base in the DATA would make the 49th domain depend on a hierarchy. If the template author prefers, `controlRecord.extends: "IslamicAccountBase"` can be introduced later as a pure generator-side optimisation without changing a single assertion here.
$meta.eventTopics: isb.deposits.<domain-slug>.<event>  — matches the existing `isb.*` topic convention. `payload` lists field names already defined on the control record or a behaviour qualifier, so AsyncAPI generation is a $ref, not a second schema.
$meta.shariahHonesty: Every `shariah` block carries reviewed:false and the literal sentence 'UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off'. Citations are to AAOIFI Shariah Standards (SS), AAOIFI Financial Accounting Standards (FAS), IFSB standards and guidance notes, and Bank Negara Malaysia's Investment Account policy document, as recorded in the Nov-2026 research (openbanking-bian-isb-research-2026-11-10/agent-investigations-shariah.md, `normative` list). A citation means 'this clause is the source of this rule', NOT 'a scholar has approved this implementation'. No field in this fragment has been reviewed by any Shariah board.

serviceDomains.name: Wadiah Safekeeping Account

fields.name: balanceMinor
fields.note: signed so a correction posting can be represented; a Wadiah balance below zero is forbidden by WAD-01

fields.name: wadiahType
fields.note: YAD_DHAMANAH = guaranteed safekeeping, the bank may use the funds and owes the amount at par. YAD_AMANAH = pure trust: funds not usable by the bank and loss without negligence falls on the depositor, so capital IS at risk. This is the one field that makes capitalAtRisk vary on a Wadiah record.

fields.name: capitalAtRisk
fields.note: queryable discriminator read by the Open Banking funds-confirmation path. Bound to wadiahType by WAD-03.

fields.name: debtorParty
fields.note: the institution owes the balance to the customer. Prevents this deposit-side domain being confused in code with the financing-side Qard Hassan Benevolent Loan.

fields.name: fundsConfirmationSupported
fields.note: false whenever capitalAtRisk is true. This is the field the CBPII path reads; see WAD-04 and DESIGN.md §7.

fields.name: hibahEligible
fields.note: eligible to RECEIVE a discretionary, unstipulated Hibah. Carries no rate, no schedule and no entitlement.

fields.name: preconditionOfAccountOpening
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 28 §2/6/2 — a free service may be given to a current-account holder only if it is NOT a precondition or a customary prerequisite for opening the account. Bundling is therefore a recorded Shariah fact, not a marketing flag.

fields.name: amountMinor
fields.note: credits positive, debits negative

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 — a usable current/Wadiah balance is a debt repayable at par; the institution cannot owe the customer a negative amount on a safekeeping arrangement.

rules.assert: absent(profitRate) && absent(interestRate) && absent(accruedInterestMinor) && absent(guaranteedReturnRate) && absent(declaredRateOfReturn) && absent(psrIahShare)
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — stipulation of ANY excess for the lender is riba, 'whether the stipulation is in writing or is part of customary practice'. BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 — field naming itself can breach the prohibition. A rate field on a Qard-family record is non-compliant before any value is stored in it.
rules.note: This is the one rule in this fragment that is checked against the CATALOG and not against a request. It fails generation, which is the point: the field must be impossible, not merely empty.

rules.assert: (wadiahType == 'YAD_DHAMANAH' && capitalAtRisk == false && lossBearer == 'INSTITUTION' && capitalAtRiskScope == 'NONE') || (wadiahType == 'YAD_AMANAH' && capitalAtRisk == true && lossBearer == 'ACCOUNT_HOLDER' && capitalAtRiskScope == 'ACCOUNT_HOLDER_CAPITAL')
rules.citation: UNSOURCED as a single clause. Derived: yad dhamanah carries a guarantee of the amount (and is treated as qard under AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1), yad amanah does not. Classification is BNM/Malaysian terminology; see `uncertain`.
DESIGN.md §7 — a funds confirmation against a capital-at-risk account must REFUSE, not answer FundsAvailable:true. The flag and the risk fact cannot disagree in the database.
ISLAMIC-MASTER-CATALOG.md — 'Gate activation on KYC + Shariah screening outcomes'. IFSB-31 Principle 9 — ongoing compliance with approved screening criteria.

AAOIFI SS 19 §9/1 — service charges on qard are limited to 'the actual amount directly spent on such services'; §9/2 excludes salaries, rent, transport and general administration. The method must be laid down by the Supervisory Board in detail.
rules.note: FLAG, not reject: the evidence amount lives in the accounting domain and may arrive after the charge. The code cannot adjudicate what counts as a direct cost — it records the comparison and raises a Shariah compliance case.

events.name: wadiah.entry.posted
events.note: consumed by Financial Crime Monitoring and AAOIFI Financial Accounting

events.name: wadiah.shariah.noncompliance.flagged
events.note: DESIGN.md §5.8 — append-only; a delete must never destroy this record

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: false for YAD_DHAMANAH (the modelled default); TRUE for YAD_AMANAH. The boolean is a stored, queryable field per record, not a constant of the domain.
shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: AAOIFI SS 19 (Loan/Qard) §10/1/1 — current accounts are loans, not deposits; the institution owns the amounts and a liability to repay at par is established.
AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — any stipulated excess to the lender is riba, including by customary practice.
AAOIFI SS 19 §5/2 — an UNSTIPULATED excess at repayment is permissible (the basis for Hibah; see the Hibah Discretionary Gift domain).
AAOIFI SS 19 §9/1–9/2 — service charges limited to actual direct cost, method laid down by the SSB.
AAOIFI SS 28 (Banking Services) §2/6/2 — free services to current-account holders must not be a precondition or customary prerequisite.

uncertain: AAOIFI has no standalone Wadiah Shariah Standard in the research set. The yad dhamanah / yad amanah split is predominantly Bank Negara Malaysia and wider Malaysian practice; AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 would reclassify a usable Wadiah balance as qard regardless of the label. ISB-WAD-03 is therefore derived, not cited, and an SSB may reject the two-value enum entirely.

Whether YAD_AMANAH belongs in a retail deposits product line at all is a product question I cannot settle: a pure-trust account whose funds the bank may not use is closer to custody than to banking. It is modelled because the master catalog calls this a 'Custody Account', and it is the honest reason capitalAtRisk is not hard-coded false.

This control record and the Qard Hassan Account control record are the same data model with a different contract label and disclosure. I did not invent a difference to justify two services. See the Qard Hassan entry's `uncertain` for the consequence.

fields.name: fundsConfirmationSupported
fields.note: the only account class in this business area where a CBPII FundsAvailable:true is a true statement, because the bank owes the amount at par

fields.name: setOffPermitted
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 3 §2/5/3 — contractual set-off against a customer account is permitted without further consent only where the balance is in the SAME currency; a different currency requires the then-prevailing rate.

fields.name: conversionRate
fields.note: the then-prevailing rate, exact; required only when sameCurrency is false

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 — the institution owes the amount at par. A qard taken from the customer cannot be negative; an overdraft on this account would be the institution lending at a charge.

rules.assert: absent(profitRate) && absent(interestRate) && absent(accruedInterestMinor) && absent(guaranteedReturnRate) && absent(declaredRateOfReturn) && absent(psrIahShare) && absent(overdraftLimitMinor)
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 (any stipulated excess is riba, including by customary practice); BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 (terminology itself can breach). overdraftLimitMinor is included deliberately: the conventional estate's sd-current-account carries it, and a generator that reuses that shape would create an interest-bearing facility by accident.
ISLAMIC-MASTER-CATALOG.md activation gate; IFSB-31 Principle 9.
AAOIFI SS 3 §2/5/3 — set-off without further consent is permitted where the account balance is of the same currency; a different currency requires the then-prevailing rate.

AAOIFI SS 3 §2/5/3 — set-off must be contractually stipulated. AAOIFI SS 3 §1 limits the procrastinating-debtor standard to solvent debtors, so an insolvency determination must block it; that determination is not held in this domain. See `uncertain`.
AAOIFI SS 19 §9/1–9/2.

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: Hard false. The institution is the debtor and owes the amount at par on demand. This is the one account class in this business area for which a funds confirmation is a truthful statement.
shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: AAOIFI SS 19 (Loan/Qard) §10/1/1 — current accounts are loans; liability to repay at par.
AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — any stipulated excess is riba, including where the stipulation is customary practice.
AAOIFI SS 19 §5/2 — unstipulated excess at repayment is permissible.
AAOIFI SS 19 §9/1–9/2 — service charges limited to actual direct cost; the method is laid down by the SSB in detail.
AAOIFI SS 3 (Procrastinating Debtor, Revised) §2/5/3 — same-currency set-off without further consent; other currency at the prevailing rate.
AAOIFI SS 3 §1 — the standard covers solvent debtors only.

uncertain: This control record is data-identical to the Wadiah Safekeeping Account record apart from the contract label, the Wadiah type enum and set-off. I report that as a finding rather than inventing a difference: under AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 a usable Wadiah balance IS a qard, so two separate service domains may be the right PRODUCT decomposition and the wrong DATA decomposition. Collapsing them into one domain with a contractType discriminator would remove a service and a repo; that call belongs to the owner and the SSB, not to me.

ISB-QRD-05 cannot be fully enforced here. AAOIFI SS 3 §1 excludes insolvent debtors and §2/6 makes default a two-condition state (demand served AND insolvency not proven), but neither the demand record nor the insolvency determination lives in this domain. The generated guard can only check the contractual permission flag; the solvency precondition must be asserted by the financing domain that initiates the set-off.

Dormancy: a DORMANT status is modelled because dormancy fees are a real Shariah question (a dormancy fee must still be actual direct cost), but no standard in the research set fixes a dormancy period, so no threshold is in the catalog.

serviceDomains.name: Mudarabah Savings Account

fields.name: investmentAccountType
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §5 / BNM PD 028-63 ¶25.2(b)(ii). A savings product is commingled and unrestricted; RESTRICTED belongs to the term domain, which carries an Investment Mandate behaviour qualifier.

fields.name: capitalAtRisk
fields.note: THE load-bearing field of this business area. Queryable, indexed, and read by the funds-confirmation path before any balance is disclosed.

fields.name: lossBearer
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 and SS 45 §3/4 make ACCOUNT_HOLDER mandatory for Mudarabah. Not a configurable product option.

fields.name: fundsConfirmationSupported
fields.note: DESIGN.md §7: a CBPII funds confirmation against this account must REFUSE. FundsAvailable:true would be a false statement about a balance the bank does not guarantee.

fields.name: capitalProtection
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 45 §2 — protection is explicitly WIDER THAN and DISTINCT FROM guarantee. Protection does not make capitalAtRisk false.

fields.name: managerLiabilityBasis
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4, SS 45 §3/4 and §3/6 — the mudarib is not liable for loss except for breach of trust, misconduct, negligence or breach of terms, and unconditional liability may not be stipulated.

fields.name: balanceMinor
fields.note: the account holder's current attributable capital. Not a liability of the bank: AAOIFI FAS 45 classifies investment accounts as QUASI-EQUITY, not liabilities. The generated README must say so, because an IFRS-trained reader will assume otherwise.

fields.name: cumulativeCapitalLossBorneMinor
fields.note: how a capital LOSS is represented without a negative balance: losses are recorded here and reduce balanceMinor, bounded by MUDS-02. AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4 requires the model to be able to represent a negative capital movement.

fields.name: profitCalculationMethodRef
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 47 §9 makes disclosure of the method of profit calculation mandatory, including the right of the client to inquire about it. IFSB-30 ¶272/¶275 require it in a machine-readable, comparable form.

fields.name: poolWeightage
fields.note: exact. The pool weightage applied to this account's balance before the profit-sharing ratio.

fields.name: expectedProfitRateBasis
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 47 §7/2 — a minimum expected profit rate may be stipulated for deployment, but neither capital nor profit may be guaranteed. BNM ¶24.5 forbids any term indicating a guaranteed return.

fields.name: riskWarningAcknowledgedAt
fields.note: BNM PD 028-63 ¶25.2(i)-(j) — the 'NOT A DEPOSIT PRODUCT' disclaimer and the 'PRINCIPAL AND RETURNS ARE NOT GUARANTEED' warning. AAOIFI SS 38 §5/4/1 requires an explicit acceptance-confirmation step, so the timestamp is a Shariah artefact, not UX telemetry.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Profit Sharing Agreement
behaviourQualifiers.note: BIAN has no profit-sharing behaviour qualifier — it has no Islamic constructs at all. This BQ exists because AAOIFI SS 13 §8/3 makes the PSR effective-dated, versioned data rather than a static product attribute, and IFSB-30 ¶276 requires it to be declared IN ADVANCE.

fields.name: effectiveTo
fields.note: null = open-ended

fields.name: psrIahShare
fields.note: a share of PROFIT. AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 — distribution must be an agreed percentage of the profit, never a lump sum and never a percentage of the capital.

fields.name: contractualMaximumMudaribShare
fields.note: IFSB GN-3 fn.13 — a unilateral increase of the mudarib share above the contractual maximum is not permitted. The contractual share is a CEILING; the realised share may be lower, including zero if waived.

fields.name: distributionType
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8 — an interim distribution is revised when actual or constructive valuation takes place. The revision is modelled as TWO postings (a reversal and a final), never an update in place.

fields.name: weightedBalanceDays
fields.note: balanceMinor x days. Bounded in practice: 10^15 minor units x 366 days stays well inside int64, but the generated repository must still reject an input that would overflow rather than wrap.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Investment Account Disclosure
behaviourQualifiers.note: BNM PD 028-63 ¶25.2 is the most concrete published field list for an Islamic investment-account disclosure; IFSB-30 ¶272–¶278 requires the same information in machine-readable form. This BQ is what the openbank-islamic sibling resource server serves.

fields.name: smoothingPolicyDisclosed
fields.note: IFSB-30 ¶277 — PER utilisation for smoothing and IRR use for covering losses 'needs to be publicised'.

fields.name: historicPerformanceYears
fields.note: BNM ¶25.2(h) requires the ACTUAL returns of the preceding 5 years, not simulations. The field records how many years of actual data exist; a new product honestly has fewer.

rules.citation: DESIGN.md §7 — 'a CBPII funds confirmation against a capital-at-risk Mudarabah investment account must REFUSE, not answer FundsAvailable:true'.
rules.note: The database cannot be put into a state where the funds-confirmation path would answer true. The sibling resource server's refusal is a second, independent check on the same two fields.
rules.test: INSERT with capitalAtRisk=true, fundsConfirmationSupported=true must be rejected by the CHECK constraint; the generated deny-test asserts the CBPII path returns the refusal error code, not 200.

rules.assert: balanceMinor >= 0 && balanceMinor == contributedCapitalMinor - redeemedCapitalMinor + cumulativeProfitCreditedMinor - cumulativeCapitalLossBorneMinor && cumulativeCapitalLossBorneMinor <= contributedCapitalMinor + cumulativeProfitCreditedMinor
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 45 §4/1/1 — partners bear risks and losses according to their shares in capital: the account holder's loss is bounded by the capital contributed. AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4 — the model must be able to represent a loss of capital.
rules.test: contributed 1000000, redeemed 0, profit credited 25000, loss borne 1025000 -> balance 0, accepted. loss borne 1025001 -> rejected. All values int64 minor units.

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 and §8/5 — the distribution is an agreed percentage of profit; a stipulated lump sum voids the contract. The two shares partition the profit exactly.
rules.test: psrIahShare 70/100 + psrMudaribShare 30/100 -> accepted (70*100 + 30*100 == 100*100). psrIahShare 7/10 + psrMudaribShare 1/4 -> rejected. Evaluated by cross-multiplication in int64; maxDenominator 1000000 keeps every product below 10^12.

rules.citation: IFSB GN-3 fn.13 — 'A unilateral increase of the Mudarib share of profits above the (maximum) percentage stated in the contract is not permitted.'
rules.test: mudarib 30/100 against maximum 30/100 -> accepted (equality allowed). mudarib 31/100 against 30/100 -> rejected.

rules.assert: count(bq.psr where effectiveFrom <= period.from && (absent(effectiveTo) || effectiveTo >= period.to)) == 1
rules.citation: IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶276 — 'under a Mudarabah contract the profit-sharing ratio must be declared in advance'. AAOIFI SS 13 §8/3 — the parties agree the ratio when the contract is concluded, with a stated validity duration.
rules.note: No allocation may be posted for a period not fully covered by exactly one agreed, in-advance PSR row. Overlapping rows are as wrong as missing ones.

rules.citation: BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 — the IFI 'shall not represent or use any terms that indicate the investment account product as principal and/or profit guaranteed or equivalent or similar to an Islamic deposit product'. The prohibition reaches the field name in the API, not only the marketing copy.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — 'No profit can be recognised or claimed unless the capital of the Mudarabah is maintained intact.' Losses are carried forward and set against future profits.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶25.2(i)-(j) (disclaimer and risk warning), AAOIFI SS 38 §5/4/1 (explicit acceptance confirmation), IFSB-30 ¶276 (PSR declared in advance), IFSB-31 Principle 9 (screening).

AAOIFI SS 45 §4/2/4 — a third-party capital-protection undertaking is valid only if the third party is administratively independent of the manager, with no direct or indirect ownership relationship above one half.
rules.note: The independence and ownership tests are facts about the provider that this service cannot verify. The record stores the reference; the determination must come from the Shariah Compliance Review domain. Reported under `uncertain`.

rules.assert: bq.allocation.distributionType == 'FINAL' -> count(bq.allocation where period == this.period && distributionType == 'PROVISIONAL_ON_ACCOUNT' && !reversed) == 0
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8 — the interim distribution 'will be revised when actual or constructive valuation takes place'; the mudarib's entitlement is absolute only after distribution. Two postings, never an update in place.

events.name: mudarabah.savings.capital.loss.attributed
events.note: the event that has no conventional counterpart: a deposit-like product reducing a customer's capital. Consumed by Customer Reference Data (notification) and AAOIFI Financial Accounting.

events.name: mudarabah.savings.funds.confirmation.refused
events.note: audited: the refusal is a deliberate, recorded behaviour, not an incidental error

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: Hard true, and the reason this business area exists. The balance is not a liability of the bank: AAOIFI FAS 45 classifies investment accounts as quasi-equity. No funds confirmation, no guarantee, no principal promise.
shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: AAOIFI SS 13 (Mudarabah, Revised) §1 Scope — expressly covers joint and special-purpose investment accounts administered on a Mudarabah basis, so SS 13 binds retail investment-account APIs.
AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4 — trust-based: the mudarib is not liable for losses except for breach of trust, misconduct, negligence or breach of terms.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 — distribution must be an agreed percentage of PROFIT, not a lump sum and not a percentage of capital.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/3 — the ratio is agreed at contract conclusion, may be changed by agreement, with a stated validity duration (hence effective-dated PSR rows).
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/5 — a stipulated lump sum for either party voids the Mudarabah.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — no profit may be recognised or claimed unless the capital is maintained intact.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8 — interim distribution on account is permitted but revised on actual or constructive valuation; neither time value nor discounting may be taken into account.

AAOIFI SS 45 (Protection of Capital and Investments) §2, §3/4, §3/6, §4/1/1, §4/2/4 — protection is distinct from guarantee; unconditional manager liability may not be stipulated; third-party protection requires administrative independence.

AAOIFI SS 47 (Rules for Calculating Profit) §7/2 and §9 — a minimum expected rate may be stipulated for deployment without guaranteeing capital or profit; the method of profit calculation must be disclosed.
AAOIFI FAS 45 — Quasi-equity (Including Investment Accounts), superseding FAS 27: investment accounts are quasi-equity, not liabilities.

IFSB GN-3 fn.12 (citing IFSB-2 ¶76) — the IIFS as mudarib may not absorb IAH investment losses except for misconduct or negligence. fn.13 — no unilateral increase of the mudarib share above the contractual maximum.

IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶272, ¶275, ¶276 — IAH entitlement to the profit-calculation method, asset allocation, strategies and smoothing mechanics, in a comparable and readily accessible form; the PSR must be declared in advance.
IFSB-22 Table 7 / Template 10 — Unrestricted PSIA qualitative and quantitative disclosures.

BNM PD 028-63 ¶8.2, ¶13.1, ¶24.5, ¶25.2, ¶27.6 — no obligation to repay in full; profit-distribution terms; prohibition on deposit-like or guarantee-like terminology; the disclosure-sheet field list; 'declared rate of return' as the correct term for the realised figure.

uncertain: AAOIFI SS 45 §4/2/4's independence test for a third-party capital-protection provider (administrative independence, no direct or indirect ownership relationship above one half) is a fact about two legal entities. ISB-MUDS-09 can only assert that a reference exists. The determination belongs to Shariah Compliance Review and I have not modelled how it is proven.

Pool weightage versus profit-sharing ratio is a jurisdictional fork. Malaysian and Gulf practice both appear in the sources, and whether weightages and a PSR are applied together or as alternatives is an SSB/product decision. Both fields are present and the generated calculation applies weightage then PSR; if a jurisdiction uses only one, the other is 1/1. I could not find a standard that fixes the order, so the order is a declared convention in the catalog, not a cited rule.

balanceBasis DEPOSIT_EQUIVALENT vs UNITISED_INVESTMENT changes what a redemption means (an amount versus a unit valuation), and a unitised account really needs unit and NAV fields. I did not model units: a NAV is a valuation with its own frequency, source and rounding policy, and inventing one would be exactly the manufactured-authority failure this phase forbids. A unitised Mudarabah product cannot be served correctly from this catalog entry as it stands.

No dormancy, no minimum balance, no tiering. BNM ¶25.2 requires eligibility criteria for profit distribution to be disclosed, but no source in the research set fixes them, so no thresholds are in the catalog.

Zakat is referenced from the disclosure BQ only (CUSTOMER_OBLIGATION_INFORMATIONAL / BANK_PAYS_ON_BEHALF). The calculation belongs to the Zakat Calculation domain in the governance area, and the nisab/hawl parameters there are genuinely contested (silver 595 g per AAOIFI SS 35 p.874 versus gold at 85 g or 87.48 g); it is not my area and I have not modelled it.

serviceDomains.name: Mudarabah Term Investment Account

fields.name: investmentAccountType
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §5; BNM PD 028-63 ¶25.2(b)(ii). RESTRICTED requires an Investment Mandate; UNRESTRICTED must not have one (MUDT-04).

fields.name: earlyRedemptionBasis

behaviourQualifiers.name: Investment Mandate

Whether the mandate is actually honoured is a question about the asset side — the pool's holdings — which lives in the treasury and financing areas, not here. AAOIFI FAS 47 (Transfer of Assets between Investment Pools) governs pool-boundary integrity, which matters when a term account's funds move between pools at rollover. profitPayoutFrequency MONTHLY/QUARTERLY on a term account looks, from the outside, exactly like an interest coupon. It is modelled because interim on-account distribution is explicitly permitted by AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8, but a payout schedule plus a stable declared rate is precisely the pattern AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 calls 'customary practice'. This is a presentation risk the data model cannot resolve and an SSB must look at.

No mention of a Tawarruq-based term deposit. The organised-tawarruq construct that many banks use for term deposits is a different contract chain and would be a different domain entry (Commodity Murabaha Tawarruq exists in the Islamic Financing area); I did not stretch this entry to cover it.

serviceDomains.name: Wakala Investment Account

fields.name: customerReference
fields.note: the principal (muwakkil). The institution is the agent (wakil).

fields.name: lossBearer
fields.note: the principal bears investment loss; the agent is liable only for wilful misconduct, negligence or breach (AAOIFI SS 46 §7/1).

fields.name: agencyFeeBasis
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 — the agency fee must be a fixed amount or a percentage of the amount INVESTED. Never a percentage of profit: that would make the wakil a partner.

fields.name: expectedProfitRate
fields.note: the Wakala-specific field. AAOIFI SS 46 §6/5 — the profit in its entirety is the principal's unless an excess above the EXPECTED profit is stipulated as the agent's performance incentive. It is an anticipation, never a promise.

fields.name: performanceIncentiveShare
fields.note: the agent's share OF THE EXCESS above expectedProfitRate only

fields.name: perReference
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6–6/7 — the agent may retain a profit-equalisation reserve FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE PRINCIPAL, and on liquidation the balance is returned to the principal. A Wakala PER therefore has no shareholder portion; see PER-07.

fields.name: investedBaseMinor
fields.note: the amount invested that the percentage was applied to; zero for FIXED_AMOUNT

fields.name: expectedProfitMinor

fields.name: agencyFeeDisclosure

rules.citation: DESIGN.md §7. AAOIFI SS 45 §3/6 — it is not permissible to stipulate that the investment manager is unconditionally liable for loss of capital, so there is no guaranteed amount to confirm.

AAOIFI SS 46 §6/5 — in a Wakala bi al-istithmar the profit in its entirety belongs to the principal; the agent earns a FEE, plus at most a stipulated share of the excess above expected profit. A profit-sharing ratio on a Wakala record would recharacterise the contract as a Mudarabah.
rules.note: The single most likely generator error in this business area: four of five account domains look alike, and a template that copies the Mudarabah shape onto Wakala produces a contract that does not exist. This lint is why the rule is in the catalog and not in a code review.

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 — the fee is a fixed amount OR a percentage of the amount invested. Exactly one, never both, never a share of profit.
rules.note: absent_value() is a runtime null check on a declared field, distinct from absent(), which is the generator-time check that the field is not declared at all.

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 — a benchmark-linked fee 'should, however, be capped and floored'.
rules.test: benchmarkLinked=true with cap 500000 and floor 100000 -> accepted; benchmarkLinked=true with cap null -> rejected; cap 100000 and floor 500000 -> rejected.

rules.assert: bq.fee_charge.basisApplied == 'PERCENT_OF_INVESTED' -> bq.fee_charge.amountMinor == ratioMul(bq.fee_charge.investedBaseMinor, bq.fee_charge.rateApplied) || bq.fee_charge.capApplied || bq.fee_charge.floorApplied
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 — the fee is a percentage of the amount invested, so the charged amount must be reproducible from the invested base and the rate. A cap or floor is the only permitted divergence and must be flagged on the row.
rules.test: investedBase 10000000, rate 75/10000 -> 75000 exactly (10000000*75/10000). investedBase 10000001, rate 75/10000 -> 75000 (truncated toward zero, remainder 75 discarded); the generated test asserts truncation, not rounding, so the behaviour is pinned.

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/5 — the agent may be entitled to all or part of any EXCESS ABOVE THE EXPECTED PROFIT as a performance incentive in addition to its fixed fee. Nothing below the expected profit is the agent's.
rules.test: expected 100000, realised 90000 -> excess 0 and incentive 0 (a shortfall never produces an incentive, and never a clawback from the principal's profit). expected 100000, realised 130000, share 20/100 -> excess 30000, incentive 6000.

rules.assert: balanceMinor >= 0 && balanceMinor == contributedCapitalMinor - redeemedCapitalMinor + cumulativeProfitCreditedMinor - cumulativeCapitalLossBorneMinor - cumulativeAgencyFeeChargedMinor - cumulativePerformanceIncentiveMinor
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 45 §4/1/1 — loss is borne according to the share in capital, bounded by the capital. The fee and the incentive are deducted from the principal's position, so they belong in the identity.
rules.test: contributed 10000000, profit 250000, fee 75000, incentive 6000, loss 0 -> balance 10169000. Any other value is rejected by the CHECK.

BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.1(a)(ii) and ¶25.2; AAOIFI SS 38 §5/4/1; IFSB-31 Principle 9.
AAOIFI SS 46 §7/1 — the agent is liable for breach of contract, which presupposes a recorded mandate to breach.

AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6–6/7 — the agent may retain a profit-equalisation reserve for the benefit of the principal; on liquidation the balance is returned to the principal.
AAOIFI SS 46 §7/1 — the agent is not liable for loss other than wilful misconduct, negligence or breach of contract.
AAOIFI SS 45 §3/4, §3/6 — manager liability limits; unconditional liability for capital loss may not be stipulated.
AAOIFI SS 47 §7/2, §9 — expected rate without guarantee; mandatory disclosure of the profit-calculation method.
AAOIFI FAS 45 — investment accounts are quasi-equity.

BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.1(a)(ii), ¶13.4, ¶24.5, ¶25.2(b)(iii), ¶27.6 — wakalah profit after agency fee and performance incentive; fee setting inputs; terminology prohibition; disclosure of the fee with clear illustrations; disclosure of average agency and performance incentive fees by tenure and type.

uncertain: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 permits a Wakala PER for the principal's benefit, returned on liquidation. IFSB GN-3's PER, by contrast, is shared between IAH and shareholders. These are not the same instrument under the same name. I have modelled the Profit Equalization Reserve domain on the IFSB GN-3 shape and added PER-07 to force a Wakala-linked reserve to have a zero shareholder portion, but whether one reserve record can honestly serve both contracts is a question for the SSB, and I would not be surprised to be told they need separate control records.

Whether a Wakala account participates in a commingled pool at all, or holds identified assets, is a product decision I could not resolve from the sources. poolReference is required because the master catalog's use case is explicitly 'attribute investment-account balances to profit-sharing pools'; an asset-identified Wakala would need a holdings structure this entry does not have.

The agency fee is modelled as charged from the principal's position (it reduces balanceMinor). Charging the fee out of the pool before attribution would produce a different and also defensible model. No source in the research set settles it, and the two differ in what the customer sees, so this is a declared convention, not a cited rule.

AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 says the fee may be benchmark-linked. A benchmark is an external rate feed with a source, an asOf and a fallback when the publication is missing. I have not modelled the feed; a benchmark-linked fee cannot be computed from this catalog entry alone.

serviceDomains.name: Profit Calculation And Distribution

fields.name: poolReference
fields.note: self-referential by design: the pool is this domain's own aggregate. See `uncertain` — the pool control record itself is NOT modelled here.

fields.name: poolContractType
fields.note: a distribution run operates on a pool whose contract type determines the waterfall: a Mudarabah pool deducts a mudarib share, a Wakala pool deducts an agency fee and at most an incentive. PCD-09 forbids mixing them.

fields.name: currency
fields.note: one run, one currency. A multi-currency pool is multiple runs; converting inside the waterfall would put a rate inside a profit calculation.

fields.name: runType
fields.note: SIMULATION satisfies the master catalog's 're-run hypothetical scenarios before changing weightings' use case. PCD-08 forbids a SIMULATION run from ever posting.

fields.name: supersedesRunRef
fields.note: a FINAL run supersedes a PROVISIONAL one by reference, through a REVERSAL. AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8: two postings, never an update in place.

fields.name: poolCapitalIntact
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — no profit may be recognised or claimed unless the capital of the Mudarabah is maintained intact. Stored on the run, not computed at read time, so the determination that licensed a distribution is auditable afterwards.

fields.name: grossPoolIncomeMinor
fields.note: signed: a pool can have a loss-making period

fields.name: perAppropriationMinor
fields.note: step 1 of the waterfall, BEFORE the mudarib share (IFSB GN-3 ¶20)

fields.name: perUtilisedForSmoothingMinor
fields.note: a drawdown of PER to smooth this period's payout. Never to cover a capital loss (IFSB-30 ¶256).

fields.name: mudaribShareMinor
fields.note: step 2. May be waived downward; may never exceed the contractual ceiling (IFSB GN-3 fn.13). Zero when poolContractType is Wakala.

fields.name: mudaribShareCeilingMinor
fields.note: ratioMul(profitAfterPer, contractualMaximumMudaribShare), stored so the waiver is visible as the gap between ceiling and actual

fields.name: agencyFeeMinor
fields.note: the Wakala analogue of the mudarib share. Zero when poolContractType is Mudarabah.

fields.name: irrAppropriationMinor
fields.note: step 3, AFTER the mudarib share, out of the profit attributable to IAH (IFSB GN-3 ¶25)

fields.name: irrUtilisedForLossMinor
fields.note: IRR drawn down to cover a loss on IAH investments — the only permitted use (IFSB GN-3 ¶20; IFSB-30 ¶256)

fields.name: roundingResidualMinor
fields.note: THE one rounding point in this business area: an int64 distributable profit cannot always be split exactly across N accounts. The residual is stored, bounded by PCD-04, and disposed of per roundingPolicy. It is never silently absorbed into the bank's share.

fields.name: roundingPolicy
fields.note: an SSB and jurisdiction choice, not a developer default. Both options keep the residual inside the IAH side; a third option that routes it to the bank is deliberately NOT offered, because that would be an unagreed increase in the mudarib's share.

fields.name: lossCarriedForwardMinor
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — losses are carried forward and set against future profits

fields.name: lossBorneByInstitutionMinor
fields.note: non-zero ONLY where the SSB has determined misconduct, negligence or breach. See PCD-06.

fields.name: smoothingJurisdictionPermitted
fields.note: BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 forbids profit smoothing and displaced-commercial-risk techniques outright, while AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 and IFSB GN-3 permit PER/IRR. Smoothing is therefore a jurisdiction-configurable capability and must never be a hard-coded behaviour.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Pool Income Allocation
behaviourQualifiers.note: IFSB-22 Template 11 and Template 12 require quantitative disclosure by CONTRACT TYPE and by ECONOMIC ACTIVITY. Both are rows here, so the regulatory report is a projection of the run rather than a separate spreadsheet.

fields.name: shariahNonCompliantIncomeMinor
fields.note: quarantined: must be excluded from distributable profit and routed to Income Purification. Never distributed to IAH, never into P&L.

fields.name: psrApplied
fields.note: null for a Wakala account: there is no profit-sharing ratio

behaviourQualifiers.name: Calculation Lineage
behaviourQualifiers.note: append-only. The master catalog's use case is 'publish calculation lineage for SSB review and customer queries'; DESIGN.md §5.8 requires append-only audit for every Shariah finding. Every input that moved a money field is a row, so the run is replayable.

fields.name: sequence
fields.note: the normative waterfall order (IFSB GN-3 ¶20/¶25). A row out of sequence is a rule violation, not a display problem.

fields.name: truncatedRemainderMinor
fields.note: whatever ratioMul discarded at this step. Recording it is what makes 'no float' an auditable claim rather than a slogan.

rules.assert: iahDistributableProfitMinor == grossPoolIncomeMinor - allocatedExpensesMinor - sum(bq.income_source.shariahNonCompliantIncomeMinor) - perAppropriationMinor + perUtilisedForSmoothingMinor - mudaribShareMinor - agencyFeeMinor - irrAppropriationMinor + irrUtilisedForLossMinor
rules.citation: IFSB GN-3 ¶20 and ¶25 — PER is appropriated out of pool profit BEFORE the allocation to shareholders and UIAH and before the mudarib share is calculated; IRR is set aside out of the profit attributable to IAH AFTER deducting the mudarib share. AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 and the SNC treatment keep non-compliant income out of distributable profit.
rules.note: The single most valuable generated test in this business area. Exact int64 equality — no tolerance, no epsilon, no rounding slack. The waterfall ORDER is not merely a convention: PER before the mudarib share makes the bank share in the smoothing, IRR after it does not.
rules.test: gross 100000000, expenses 5000000, snc 0, perAppropriation 2000000, perUtilised 0, mudaribShare 18600000, agencyFee 0, irrAppropriation 1000000, irrUtilised 0 -> iahDistributable 73400000. Change any single input by 1 minor unit and the assertion must fail.

rules.assert: mudaribShareMinor <= mudaribShareCeilingMinor && mudaribShareCeilingMinor == ratioMul(grossPoolIncomeMinor - allocatedExpensesMinor - perAppropriationMinor + perUtilisedForSmoothingMinor, contractualMaximumMudaribShare)
rules.citation: IFSB GN-3 fn.13 — no unilateral increase of the mudarib share above the contractual maximum. The share may be waived DOWNWARD, which is why the assertion is <= and the ceiling is stored.
rules.test: profitAfterPer 93000000, contractualMaximumMudaribShare 20/100 -> ceiling 18600000. mudaribShare 18600000 accepted; 18600001 rejected; 0 accepted (full waiver).

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 — no profit can be recognised or claimed unless the capital is maintained intact; losses are carried forward and set against future profits. A mudarib share on a loss-making period is a fee on a loss, which the Mudarabah contract does not permit.
rules.note: The agency fee is set to zero here too, which is the STRICTER reading. AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 makes the Wakala fee a fee on the amount invested, not on profit, so a literal reading would let it stand in a loss period. Flagged in `uncertain`.

rules.citation: UNSOURCED as a Shariah clause; it is the arithmetic consequence of distributing an int64 across N holders without a float. AAOIFI SS 47 §8/2 is the nearest hook: institutions must avoid methods of profit calculation or distribution that are misleading.
rules.note: The bound `roundingResidualMinor < accountCount` is what stops a rounding residual being used as a silent skim: with a correct largest-remainder allocation each account is short by at most one minor unit, so the residual cannot exceed the number of accounts.
rules.test: iahDistributed 1000000, accountCount 3, allocations 333334 + 333333 + 333333 -> residual 0, accepted. allocations 333333 x3 -> residual 1, accepted. allocations 300000 x3 -> residual 100000, rejected (>= accountCount).

rules.citation: BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — 'The IFI must not implement profit smoothing practices or displaced commercial risk (DCR) techniques.' This directly contradicts AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 and IFSB GN-3, which permit PER/IRR. The contradiction is real and is resolved by configuration with a named authority, never by a default in code.

IFSB GN-3 fn.12 citing IFSB-2 ¶76 — 'the IIFS as Mudarib is not permitted to absorb losses incurred on the IAH's investment as this is not Shari'ah compliant, except in the case of misconduct or negligence'. AAOIFI SS 13 §4/4 and SS 45 §3/4 to the same effect.
rules.note: A commercially tempting kindness — the bank quietly covering a bad month — is a Shariah violation. The code cannot decide that misconduct occurred; it refuses the posting until the Shariah Compliance Review domain has recorded a determination.

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 13 §8/7 (capital intact); IFSB-30 Principle 18 ¶272 (IAH entitled to the method); DESIGN.md §5.8 (append-only audit). Non-compliant income must be routed to purification before anything is declared.
UNSOURCED as a Shariah clause; it is the containment rule the master catalog's scenario use case requires. A simulation that can post is an unaudited distribution.

AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 (mudarib takes a share of profit) versus AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 and §6/5 (the wakil takes a fee on the amount invested plus at most a share of the excess). A pool cannot do both at once, and a run that charged both would be charging twice for one role.
AAOIFI SS 13 §8/8 — an interim distribution on account is revised when actual or constructive valuation takes place. Modelled as two postings; the provisional run is reversed, never edited.

UNSOURCED. A guard against the failure mode no standard names: every ratioMul truncation discards a remainder, and if those remainders are not accounted for, money leaves the waterfall without a destination. FLAG rather than reject, because the bound is heuristic — see `uncertain`.

events.name: profit.loss.carried.forward
events.note: the event with no conventional counterpart: a distribution run that distributes nothing because the pool lost money

events.name: profit.snc.income.quarantined
events.note: consumed by Income Purification and Shariah Compliance Review; append-only

shariah.contractTypeNote: A distribution run is not itself a contract. It operates on a pool whose contract type is per-pool, which is why poolContractType is a stored, queryable field and PCD-09 forbids the two waterfalls being mixed. DESIGN.md §7's ContractType enum has no value for a process domain, so Mudarabah is recorded here as the dominant case.

shariah.review: UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off
standards: IFSB GN-3 (Guidance Note on the Practice of Smoothing the Profits Payout to Investment Account Holders, Dec 2010) ¶20, ¶25 — the normative waterfall order: PER before the allocation to shareholders and UIAH and before the mudarib share; IRR after deducting the mudarib share, usable only to cover losses on UIAH investments.
IFSB GN-3 ¶26, ¶27 — PER collectively belongs to IAH and shareholders; IRR is created in the equity of IAH.
IFSB GN-3 ¶28 — IAH agree in advance on the proportion of their income that may be appropriated to each reserve.

IFSB GN-3 fn.12 (citing IFSB-2 ¶76) — the IIFS as mudarib may not absorb IAH investment losses except for misconduct or negligence. fn.13 — no unilateral increase of the mudarib share above the contractual maximum.

AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1, §8/7, §8/8, §9/6 — profit as an agreed percentage; capital intact before recognition; interim distribution revised on actual or constructive valuation; no gift or donation out of Mudarabah funds.
AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1, §6/5 — the Wakala alternative: a fee on the amount invested plus at most a share of the excess above expected profit.
AAOIFI SS 47 §8/2, §9 — no misleading or deceptive methods of profit calculation or distribution; the method must be disclosed and open to client inquiry.
AAOIFI FAS 35 — Risk Reserves, the standard governing PER and IRR. AAOIFI FAS 45 — Quasi-equity (Including Investment Accounts).

IFSB-30 Principle 15 ¶256 — the PER shall not be used to compensate for a loss in capital; the IRR serves that purpose. Principle 18 ¶272, ¶276–¶278 — IAH information rights, PSR in advance, publication of smoothing and of material policy changes.
IFSB-22 Template 10, Template 11, Template 12 — PSIA quantitative disclosures by contract and by economic activity, with the PER split between shareholders and IAH and the IRR balance as line items.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — profit smoothing and DCR techniques are forbidden in Malaysia; ¶27.6 — 'declared rate of return' is the correct term for the realised figure.

uncertain: THE BIGGEST GAP IN MY AREA: there is no pool control record. This domain's catalog entry models the RUN, and a run references a pool by string. A pool has its own identity, asset side, opening and closing equity, carried-forward losses, participating accounts and FAS 47 transfer rules. A clean design would make 'Investment Pool' a tenth service domain in this business area — a Maintain or Administer pattern on an 'Investment Pool' asset type — and the master catalog does not have one. I did not add a domain to the catalog because the task says to read the domain list rather than invent it, so I am reporting it instead: the 48-domain decomposition has a hole where the pool should be, and lossCarriedForwardMinor on a run is a per-run number with nowhere authoritative to accumulate.

PCD-03 forces the Wakala agency fee to zero in a loss period. That is my stricter reading, not a cited rule: AAOIFI SS 46 §5/1 makes the fee a charge on the amount invested rather than on profit, so a literal reading would let the fee stand and deepen the IAH's loss. I chose the reading that cannot overcharge a customer and I am flagging it, because an SSB may well say the fee is due regardless.

PCD-11's bound (sum of truncated remainders <= residual + accountCount) is heuristic. I could derive a tight bound only for the final allocation step, not for a chain of ratioMul operations whose remainders partly cancel. It is therefore a FLAG, and the generated test pins current behaviour rather than proving a limit. A tight bound needs the waterfall's step count, which is data the template has.

Expense allocation to the pool (allocatedExpensesMinor) is modelled as one number. Which expenses may be charged to IAH funds at all is a contested Shariah question — AAOIFI SS 19 §9/2 excludes indirect expenses from qard service charges, and BNM ¶27.6 requires allocated expenses to be disclosed as a line item — but no source in the research set gives a closed list for a Mudarabah pool. One opaque number is the honest shape; a breakdown would imply an authority I do not have.

The run is single-currency by construction. A real pool holding assets in several currencies needs a conversion step, and a conversion rate inside a profit waterfall is the single most dangerous place in this design (DESIGN.md §6). I kept it out: multi-currency pools are not servable from this entry.

Pakistan's State Bank caps for these reserves (reportedly IRR <= 10% and PER <= 30% of Islamic Banking Equity, with a minimum 75% of weighted-average gross yield on PKR savings from 1 Jan 2025) appear in the research only via secondary sources. They are NOT in this catalog as numbers. See the reserve domains' jurisdictionCapShare field.

rules.citation: IFSB GN-3 ¶28 — IAH agree in advance on the proportion of their income that may be appropriated to the reserve. More than the agreed proportion is an unagreed withholding of the customer's profit.
rules.test: poolProfitBeforeAppropriation 95000000, contractualMaxAppropriationShare 25/1000 -> maximum 2375000. amount 2000000 accepted; 2375001 rejected.

rules.citation: IFSB-30 Principle 15 ¶256 — 'The PER shall not be used to compensate for the loss in capital, and for this purpose a special type of reserve is used, which is the investment risk reserve.' The enum has exactly one value so that the wrong purpose is unrepresentable, not merely rejected.
UNSOURCED as a clause; a reserve cannot be drawn below zero without becoming a loan from the shareholders to the IAH, which no source in the research set permits.

BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 — 'The IFI must not implement profit smoothing practices or displaced commercial risk (DCR) techniques.' PER/IRR is a jurisdictional fork, not a feature: the capability must be switchable off entirely, and in Malaysia it is off.

Jurisdiction-specific and NOT verified in the research (the Pakistan caps came from secondary sources). FLAG, and only when a cap has been configured with a cited source. No cap number is in this catalog.

That is not IFSB GN-3's shared PER. Keeping both under one control record requires this rule; see `uncertain`.

uncertain: AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6-6/7's Wakala PER and IFSB GN-3's shared PER are arguably two different instruments wearing one name: the Wakala reserve belongs wholly to the principal and is returned on liquidation, while the GN-3 reserve is shared with shareholders and forgone on exit. I modelled one control record with poolContractType plus PER-07 rather than two domains, because the catalog has one Profit Equalization Reserve domain. An SSB may split them, and that would be a new catalog entry, not a code change.

Whether the IAH's PER portion is forgone or returned on termination is contract terms, and the two cited sources point opposite ways (IFSB GN-3 ¶28 / IFSB-30 ¶254 versus AAOIFI SS 46 §6/7). onTerminationIahPortionTreatment therefore has no default. A generator that defaults it would be choosing a Shariah position.

The iah/shareholder split RATIO on each appropriation is not modelled. I store the two amounts per row and assert they sum, but what determines the split is not in the sources I have — it may follow the PSR, the pool's equity proportions, or a separate contractual term. Storing a ratio I cannot cite would be inventing one.

jurisdictionCapShare is deliberately empty. The Pakistan caps (PER <= 30% of Islamic Banking Equity, IRR <= 10%) appear in the research only through secondary sources, and the cap base, Islamic Banking Equity, is computed in the IFSB Regulatory Reporting domain, not here. PER-06 flags rather than rejects, and only when a cap has been configured with a cited source.

A smoothed payout is, economically, closer to a fixed return than an unsmoothed one. Whether a given smoothing practice crosses from permitted equalisation into an implied guarantee is a judgement that no field can hold. The model records the mechanics so the SSB can see them; it cannot decide them.

serviceDomains.name: Hibah Discretionary Gift

fields.name: targetContractType
fields.note: a Hibah may only go to a non-capital-at-risk deposit. Paying a 'gift' to a Mudarabah or Wakala investment-account holder would be a return outside the agreed profit mechanism, i.e. a disguised guarantee. Enforced by HIB-02.

fields.name: discretionBasis
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 19 §5/2 — an UNSTIPULATED excess at repayment is permissible. The permission rests entirely on the award being unstipulated, so the only permitted basis is the institution's own discretion.

fields.name: contractuallyStipulated
fields.note: pinned false with a single-value CHECK. AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — a stipulated excess is riba whether stipulated in writing or by customary practice. A true here is not a bad record, it is a prohibited product.

fields.name: fundingSource
fields.note: AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 — the mudarib may not make a loan, gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds. A Hibah funded from the IAH pool would take investment-account holders' money to pay depositors.

fields.name: approvalAuthorityRef
fields.note: the internal body that exercised the discretion, recorded per award

fields.name: cadenceReviewFlag
fields.note: set by HIB-06 when this account's award history starts to look like a customary entitlement. A flag for the Shariah compliance function, never a block on the payment.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Award Decision
behaviourQualifiers.note: append-only decision trail: who exercised the discretion, on what date, with what SSB reference. The discretion is the Shariah basis for the award, so it must be evidenced per award and not per product.

behaviourQualifiers.name: Cadence Observation
behaviourQualifiers.note: the detection surface for HIB-06. Stored rather than computed on the fly so that a referral to the SSB carries the evidence that triggered it.

fields.name: impliedEffectiveRate
fields.note: computed FOR REVIEW ONLY and never shown to the customer or used to size a future award: doing either would convert the gift into the rate the prohibition is about.

fields.name: thresholdPeriodsConfigured
fields.note: SSB configuration. There is no default in this catalog, because a threshold is a Shariah judgement about when practice becomes custom.

rules.assert: contractuallyStipulated == false && derivedFromRate == false && derivedFromSchedule == false && discretionBasis == 'INSTITUTION_DISCRETION_UNSTIPULATED'
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — stipulation of any excess for the lender is riba, 'whether the excess is stipulated at the time of the contract or while determining the period of delay ... and, further, whether the stipulation is in writing or is part of customary practice'. AAOIFI SS 19 §5/2 — an unstipulated excess at repayment is permissible, which is the only ground this whole domain stands on.
rules.note: Three single-value CHECK constraints. A stipulated Hibah is not a validation error to be reported to a user; it is a product the database must be unable to hold.

rules.citation: Derived from AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 and §8/5 (an investment-account holder's return must come from the agreed share of profit, and a stipulated lump sum voids the Mudarabah) together with BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 (nothing may represent an investment account as guaranteed). A discretionary gift to an IAH is a return outside the agreed mechanism and reads as a top-up guarantee.
rules.note: Marked derived, not cited: I did not find a clause that says in terms 'no hibah to an investment account'. I believe the inference is sound and I am flagging that it IS an inference.

rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 — the mudarib may not make a loan, gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds. Funding a depositor's gift from the investment pool spends the IAH's money on someone else's benefit.

rules.assert: absent(hibahRate) && absent(profitRate) && absent(interestRate) && absent(awardSchedule) && absent(declaredRateOfReturn) && absent(guaranteedAmountMinor) && absent(expectedHibahMinor)
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 as above; BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 — terminology itself can breach.
rules.note: The reason this domain's catalog entry carries no rate field of any kind: a rate the code can store is a rate the product can promise. impliedEffectiveRate exists ONLY on the Cadence Observation behaviour qualifier, as review evidence, and HIB-06 is what keeps it there.

rules.assert: status == 'PAID' -> (exists(approvedAt) && count(bq.decision where decisionType == 'APPROVED') >= 1 && exists(ssbApprovalRef) && count(bq.posting) >= 1)
rules.citation: AAOIFI SS 19 §5/2 — the permission rests on the award being a genuine exercise of discretion, so the discretion must be evidenced per award. AAOIFI SS 19 §9/1 to the same effect for the method being laid down by the Supervisory Board in detail.

AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — the prohibition explicitly reaches a stipulation that 'is part of customary practice'. This is the one Shariah risk in this domain that is not a field at all but a PATTERN over time: a gift paid every month at a stable effective rate has become an expectation, and no single award record is wrong.
rules.note: FLAG, and deliberately so. The code raises a Shariah Compliance Review case with the cadence evidence attached; it must not block the payment, because whether custom has formed is a judgement for the SSB and not for a threshold. The threshold itself is configuration with no default in this catalog — see `uncertain`.

rules.citation: DESIGN.md §5.8 — append-only audit. A reversal is a compensating posting, never a deleted row: the award happened and the record of it must survive.

events.name: hibah.award.paid

events.name: hibah.cadence.referred

shariah.capitalAtRiskNote: False, and necessarily so: HIB-02 forbids a Hibah to a capital-at-risk account.

standards: AAOIFI SS 19 (Loan/Qard) §5/2 — an unstipulated excess at repayment is permissible. This is the entire Shariah basis for the domain.
AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 — a stipulated excess is riba, including where the stipulation is in writing OR is part of customary practice.
AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 — a current account is a loan to the institution, which is why an excess paid on it is governed by the qard rules at all.
AAOIFI SS 19 §9/1 — the method must be laid down by the Supervisory Board of the institution in detail.
AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 — the mudarib may not make a loan, gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds.
BNM PD 028-63 ¶24.5 — nothing may represent a product as principal or profit guaranteed or equivalent to a deposit.

uncertain: THE HARDEST THING IN MY AREA, and I want to be plain about it: this domain is Shariah-compliant only as long as nobody relies on it. Every individual award can be unstipulated, discretionary and properly approved, and the product can still drift into a customary entitlement, which AAOIFI SS 19 §4/1 catches in terms. HIB-06 detects the drift and refers it; it cannot decide it, and I have deliberately not given thresholdPeriodsConfigured a default. A generator that shipped a default here would be making a Shariah ruling in a config file.

HIB-02 (no Hibah to a capital-at-risk account) is DERIVED, not cited. I did not find a clause stating it directly. It follows from AAOIFI SS 13 §8/1 and §8/5 and BNM ¶24.5, and I think it is right, but an SSB might permit a hibah to an IAH in specific circumstances and then this rule is wrong.

impliedEffectiveRate is computed on the review surface and I am uneasy about it existing at all. The argument for it: a referral without evidence is not actionable. The argument against: the number is one `GET` away from a customer-facing channel, and once a customer sees it the gift has become a rate. The compromise is that it lives only on the Cadence Observation behaviour qualifier and only the referral event carries it, to Shariah Compliance Review. If the openbank-islamic sibling ever exposes it on a customer path, that is a defect and the generated authorization deny-test should say so.

Hibah on a Wadiah account is included because the master catalog places this domain alongside the Wadiah and Qard Hassan products, but under AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 a usable Wadiah balance IS a qard, so the Wadiah case may be the Qard case wearing a different name. Same open question as the two account domains.

Nothing here models tax or withholding on a gift, and nothing models a Hibah in kind (a non-cash gift). Both exist in practice. amountMinor plus a currency cannot express a gift of goods, and I did not invent a shape for one.

areaLevelFindings: MISSING DOMAIN — Investment Pool. This business area models accounts, runs, reserves and a gift, and has no control record for the POOL that every one of them references by string. A pool has identity, an asset side, opening and closing equity, carried-forward losses, participating accounts and AAOIFI FAS 47 transfer rules. Without it, lossCarriedForwardMinor has nowhere authoritative to accumulate, a mandate breach cannot be checked against holdings, and the IRR's loss absorption cannot be reconciled with the accounts' loss attribution. DESIGN.md §8 already provides for invented entries ('the missing account/transaction/balance/statement/position domains are new catalog entries'); an 'Investment Pool' entry (pattern Maintain or Administer) belongs in the same list. I did not add it, because the task told me to read the domain list rather than invent it, and because it affects the domain count that other agents are working from.

TWO DOMAINS, ONE DATA MODEL — Wadiah Safekeeping Account and Qard Hassan Account are data-identical apart from the contract label, the Wadiah type enum and set-off. Under AAOIFI SS 19 §10/1/1 a usable Wadiah balance is a qard. This may be the right product decomposition and the wrong data decomposition; collapsing them would remove a repo. Owner and SSB call, not mine.

THE CAPITAL-AT-RISK SURFACE IS FOUR FIELDS, NOT ONE. capitalAtRisk (the queryable discriminator), capitalAtRiskScope (whose capital), lossBearer (who bears it) and fundsConfirmationSupported (what the API must do about it), with a db-check in every account domain tying the last to the first. DESIGN.md §7's funds-confirmation refusal is therefore enforced in the database, not only in the resource server: there is no row the CBPII path could read that would license a FundsAvailable:true.

THE SINGLE MOST LIKELY GENERATOR BUG in this area is cross-contract field bleed: five account domains look alike, and copying the Mudarabah shape onto Wakala invents a profit-sharing ratio that the contract does not have, while copying the PER shape onto the IRR invents a shareholder portion that IFSB GN-3 ¶27 forbids. Both are caught by generator-lint rules (ISB-WKL-02, ISB-IRR-05) that assert a field is ABSENT from the catalog entry. They fail generation rather than a request, which is the only place such a check is worth anything.

ONE ROUNDING POINT, DECLARED. The only place a generated money path in this area rounds is the allocation of an int64 distributable profit across N accounts. It is an explicit field (roundingResidualMinor), bounded by a rule (ISB-PCD-04: 0 <= residual < accountCount), disposed of by an SSB-chosen policy whose options all keep the residual on the IAH side, and every intermediate truncation is recorded on the Calculation Lineage behaviour qualifier. 'No float' is only an auditable claim if the discarded remainders have a home.

ISO 4217 EXPONENTS ARE PART OF THE TEST DATA, not a footnote. ISB-MUDT-02's generated test uses BHD (exponent 3) deliberately, because a test written in a 2-decimal currency passes against a hardcoded x100 bug. The currency field carries the exponent; no generated code converts.

PER/IRR ARE JURISDICTION-GATED DATA, NOT A FEATURE FLAG IN CODE. AAOIFI SS 46 §6/6 and IFSB GN-3 permit them; BNM PD 028-63 ¶13.5 forbids profit smoothing and DCR outright. Both reserve domains and the distribution run carry jurisdictionPermitted plus a jurisdictionRef, and a false value disables every appropriation and utilisation. No cap NUMBERS are in this catalog: the Pakistan figures reached the research only through secondary sources.

NO FIELD IN THIS FRAGMENT HAS BEEN REVIEWED BY ANY SHARIAH BOARD. Every shariah block says so. The citations identify the clause a rule came from; they do not transfer its authority to this design. Nine `uncertain` lists name what I could not model, and the two rules I derived rather than cited (ISB-WAD-03, ISB-HIB-02) say so in the rule itself.
